import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))

# Create subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))

# 1. Income distribution by education level
income_edu = df.groupby('Education')['Income'].agg(['mean', 'median', 'count']).reset_index()
income_edu = income_edu.sort_values('mean', ascending=False)

bars1 = axes[0, 0].bar(income_edu['Education'], income_edu['mean'], color=plt.cm.Set3(np.arange(len(income_edu))))
axes[0, 0].set_title('Average Income by Education Level', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Average Income ($)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars1:
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[0, 0].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 1000,
                   f'${height:,.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)

# 2. Spending categories comparison
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 
                 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_totals = df[spending_cols].sum()
spending_labels = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweet', 'Gold']

colors2 = plt.cm.Paired(np.arange(len(spending_labels)))
wedges, texts, autotexts = axes[0, 1].pie(spending_totals, labels=spending_labels, autopct='%1.1f%%',
                                          colors=colors2, startangle=90)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Total Spending by Category', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)

# Make autotexts white for better visibility
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

# 3. Purchase channels comparison
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
purchase_totals = df[purchase_cols].sum()
purchase_labels = ['Web Purchases', 'Catalog Purchases', 'Store Purchases']

x_pos = np.arange(len(purchase_labels))
bars3 = axes[1, 0].bar(x_pos, purchase_totals, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1'])
axes[1, 0].set_title('Total Purchases by Channel', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Purchase Channel', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Number of Purchases', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_xticks(x_pos)
axes[1, 0].set_xticklabels(purchase_labels, rotation=0)

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars3:
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[1, 0].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 50,
                   f'{int(height):,}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)

# 4. Customer demographics heatmap
# Create age groups
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']
age_bins = [18, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 100]
age_labels = ['18-29', '30-39', '40-49', '50-59', '60-69', '70+']
df['Age_Group'] = pd.cut(df['Age'], bins=age_bins, labels=age_labels, right=False)

# Create income groups
income_bins = [0, 30000, 50000, 70000, 90000, 200000]
income_labels = ['<30k', '30-50k', '50-70k', '70-90k', '>90k']
df['Income_Group'] = pd.cut(df['Income'], bins=income_bins, labels=income_labels)

# Create cross-tabulation
heatmap_data = pd.crosstab(df['Age_Group'], df['Income_Group'], normalize='index') * 100

sns.heatmap(heatmap_data, annot=True, fmt='.1f', cmap='YlOrRd', 
            cbar_kws={'label': 'Percentage (%)'}, ax=axes[1, 1])
axes[1, 1].set_title('Customer Distribution: Age vs Income Groups', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Income Group ($)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Age Group', fontsize=12)

# Adjust layout
plt.suptitle('Customer Segmentation Analysis: Demographics and Spending Behavior', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.close()
